note: English passages a translator found ambiguous. For the owner to settle in the English (Standard §1 rule 1); translations follow the English as written until then.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar's words are "taiḥ bhujyatē sukhēna anubhūyatē iti bhōjanam", "He is enjoyed with delight by His devotees." The Lord makes the objects of this world fit to be enjoyed, and when His devotee rises above the desire for worldly things, He becomes Himself the object of their enjoyment. Nammazhwar says that for him, the Lord is the food he eats, the water he drinks, and the betel he chews (uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr thinnum veṭṭilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan).
concerns.note: Tamil pasuram line (Nammazhwar) quoted only in romanisation; Hindi transliterated via the Tamil (உண்ணும் சோறு பருகு நீர் தின்னும் வெற்றிலையும் எல்லாம் கண்ணன்) per Standard §3.3; verify the line against the authoritative Tiruvaymozhi text.

concerns.english: As soon as Bali poured the water to seal his gift of three steps into the hands of the dwarf, the dwarf was no longer a dwarf. The Lord grew to cover the three worlds: the earth became His foot, the sky His head, and the sun and the moon His eyes. The Harivamsa describes the beauty of this growth in relation to the sun and the stars. Andal begins the third pasuram of the Thiruppavai with "the great one who grew and measured the worlds" (ōṅgi ulagaḷanda uttaman).
concerns.note: Andal's Tiruppavai 3 line quoted only in romanisation; Hindi transliterated via the Tamil (ஓங்கி உலகளந்த உத்தமன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad says, "This Self is honey to all beings" (ayamātmā sarvēṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu). Periyazhwar calls Him "the Lord who is sweeter than honey" (thēnil iniya pirānē). From the next name, Sri Bhattar describes the Lord's six divine qualities: knowledge, strength, lordship, valour, power, and splendour.
concerns.note: Periyazhwar line 'thēnil iniya pirānē' quoted only in romanisation; Hindi transliterated via the Tamil (தேனில் இனிய பிரானே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: When the Milk Ocean was churned, Sri Mahalakshmi rose from it. While all the devas waited and watched, She chose the Lord, and He welcomed Her to reside on His chest. Nammazhwar describes Her declaring that She will not leave Him even for a moment (agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl maṅgai uṟai mārbā).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar line 'agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl maṅgai uṟai mārbā' transliterated via the Tamil (அகலகில்லேன் இறையும் என்று அலர்மேல் மங்கை உறை மார்பா); Standard §3.3 gives no Hindi rule for intervocalic க, so the quoted pronunciation (ग) was followed; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The word gō means the earth, cows, speech, or the Vedas. The Lord says in the Mahabharata, "Long ago I found the earth, which had gone down to the netherworld, and so I am called Govinda." Sri Bhattar explains the name here as "the one who receives the praise (gō) of the devas" for His help in the Hamsa incarnation. In the Thiruppavai, Andal calls Him "Govinda, who has no deficiency" (kuṟai onṟum illādha gōvindā), and says that our relationship with Him can never be broken.
concerns.note: Andal's Tiruppavai line 'kuṟai onṟum illādha gōvindā' transliterated via the Tamil (குறை ஒன்றும் இல்லாத கோவிந்தா); verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Even in Matsya Avataram, He adorns the Vaijayanti Mala, which indicates Parabrahma Swaroopam.
concerns.note: Tiruppanazhwar's closing line of Amalanadipiran 'en amudhinaik kaṇḍa kaṇgaḷ maṟṟonṟinaik kāṇāvē' transliterated via the Tamil (என் அமுதினைக் கண்ட கண்கள் மற்றொன்றினைக் காணாவே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The name comes from the root vṛ, "to cover". The Lord remains hidden from those in whom tamas dominates; only devotion reveals Him. Just as the sun creates the clouds that hide it from us, and yet its own light is untouched by them, our ignorance hides the Lord from us while He remains as radiant as ever. Nammazhwar praises Him as the one who blessed him with knowledge and devotion free from confusion (mayarvaṟa madhinalam aruḷinan).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar line 'mayarvaṟa madhinalam aruḷinan' transliterated via the Tamil (மயர்வற மதிநலம் அருளினன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar describes how the Lord, as the inner controller of Rudra, burnt down the three cities of the asuras and gave knowledge to the devas (puram oru mūnṟu eritthu amararkkum aṟivu iyandhu). By destroying their cities, He removed the fears that came upon the devas.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar line 'puram oru mūnṟu eritthu amararkkum aṟivu iyandhu' transliterated via the Tamil (புரம் ஒரு மூன்று எரித்து அமரர்க்கும் அறிவு இயந்து) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Andal sings in the Thiruppavai of the Lord who "went there and destroyed beautiful Lanka in the south" (senṟu angu then ilangai seṟṟāi). Periyazhwar sings of how He went and cut off the thousand arms of Banasura. The Lord's valour is always used to go to His devotees' aid.
concerns.note: Andal's Tiruppavai line 'senṟu angu then ilangai seṟṟāi' transliterated via the Tamil (சென்று அங்கு தென் இலங்கை செற்றாய்) as quoted; the authoritative text may read 'அங்குத் தென்'; verify.

concerns.english: This naama occurred earlier as the 48th and the 198th naamas. Here, in the description of the divine form of Para Vasudeva, it refers to the beauty of His lotus-like navel. Thiruppaanazhwar sings of "the beauty of the navel that gave birth to Brahma" (ayanaip paḍaitthadhōr ezhil undhi).
concerns.note: Tiruppanazhwar line 'ayanaip paḍaitthadhōr ezhil undhi' transliterated via the Tamil (அயனைப் படைத்ததோர் எழில் உந்தி); verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Thiruppaanazhwar sings of "those great, long eyes with red streaks, which have driven me mad" (seyya vāya aiyō ennaic cindhai kavarndhadhuvē). In the Sundara Kandam, Hanuman describes Rama as "rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ", Rama with eyes like lotus petals.
concerns.note: Possible English-source mismatch: the gloss describes the Lord's eyes, but the quoted line 'seyya vāya aiyō ennaic cindhai kavarndhadhuvē' ('red mouth ... has stolen my mind') appears to close Amalanadipiran's verse on His mouth; the eyes verse ends '... ennaip pēdhaimai seydhanavē'. Translated as written; owner to check which line is intended.

concerns.english: The one who thinks He is prosperous only when His devotees are prosperous.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar line 'vīṟṟirundhu Ezh ulagum thanik kōl sella ALum ammān' transliterated via the Tamil (வீற்றிருந்து ஏழுலகும் தனிக்கோல் செல்ல ஆளும் அம்மான்); verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Garuda is said to be the embodiment of the Vedas, and so the Lord's vehicle is worthy of the highest reverence. Nammazhwar calls the Lord "the one who rides on the bird" (puḷḷūrdhi).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation in this batch (items 4 'puḷḷūrdhi', 27 'thiruc ceyya kamalak kaṇṇum sevvāyum sevvadiyum', 35 'etthiṟam! uralinōdu iṇaindhirundhu Engiya eḷivē') transliterated via the Tamil (புள்ளூர்தி; திருச் செய்ய கமலக் கண்ணும் செவ்வாயும் செவ்வடியும்; எத்திறம்! உரலினோடு இணைந்திருந்து ஏங்கிய எளிவே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar sings of the Lord "whose soft feet are pressed by the Lady of the lotus and by the Lady of the earth" (malar magaḷ maṟṟum maṇ magaḷ pidikkum mel adiyān).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation in this batch (items 2, 12, 26, 28: 'malar magaḷ maṟṟum maṇ magaḷ pidikkum mel adiyān', 'palapala māya mayakkugaḷāl inbuṟum iv viḷaiyāṭṭudaiyān', 'viṇṇavarkku eṇṇal ariyān', 'kākkum iyalvinan kaṇṇa perumān') transliterated via the Tamil per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Because He is complete in every respect, there is no room in Him for likes and dislikes, wants and desires. Thiruvalluvar describes the Lord as "the one who has neither desire nor aversion" (vēṇḍudal vēṇḍāmai ilān). Meditating on this naama helps us move towards that state ourselves.
concerns.note: Thiruvalluvar (Kural 4) phrase 'vēṇḍudal vēṇḍāmai ilān' transliterated via the Tamil (வேண்டுதல் வேண்டாமை இலான்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar quotes the Bala Kandam: "The son of king Dasaratha, endowed with world-wide renown" (pṛthuśrīḥ pārthivātmajaḥ), and "Among them, Rama was the most renowned in the world" (tēṣām atiyaśā lōkē rāmaḥ). Nammazhwar calls Him "the one whose fame has no equal" (nigar il pugazhāy).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (items 13 'nigar il pugazhāy', 23 'tēnum pālum kannalum amudumāgit tittippa') transliterated via the Tamil (நிகர் இல் புகழாய்; தேனும் பாலும் கன்னலும் அமுதுமாகித் தித்திப்ப) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: This naama occurs again as the 821st naama. Sri Bhattar explains that He knows that He is the inner controller of everything, and that He is Himself the best dharma, the best means, and the best goal. Thirumangai Azhwar addresses Him as "You who know everything in the world" (ulagattu ellām aṟivīr).
concerns.note: Thirumangai Azhwar phrase 'ulagattu ellām aṟivīr' transliterated via the Tamil (உலகத்து எல்லாம் அறிவீர்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar explains that the Lord is proclaimed by the voice of the Upanishads. Nammazhwar sings of "Narayana, the Lord of all the seven worlds, who is praised by the Vedas" (nāraṇan muzhu ēzhulagukkum nāthan vēda mayan). Sri Sankara adds that His voice is deep and sonorous, like the rumbling of the rain cloud.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (items 6 'nāraṇan muzhu ēzhulagukkum nāthan vēda mayan', 12 'maiyal seidu ennai manam kavarndānē', 24 'parandha taṇ paravai uḷ nīr thoṟum paranduḷan') transliterated via the Tamil (நாரணன் முழு ஏழுலகுக்கும் நாதன் வேத மயன்; மையல் செய்து என்னை மனம் கவர்ந்தானே; பரந்த தண் பரவை உள் நீர் தொறும் பரந்துளன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar lists the many acts of the Lord during the churning: churning the ocean, supporting the mountain, overcoming the enemies, and distributing the nectar. Nammazhwar marvels at "the skill of the one who churned the ocean and left in such a way that the devas ate the nectar while the asuras were left out" (kūḍi nīraik kaḍaindavāṟum amudam dēvar uṇṇa asurargaḷai vīḍum vaṇṇaṅgaḷ seidu pōna vittagamum).
concerns.note: Tamil phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 0 Nammazhwar 'kūḍi nīraik kaḍaindavāṟum … vittagamum', item 7 Andal 'kanṟu mēyttu inidu ugandha kāḷāy', item 17 Nammazhwar 'neṟi ellām eḍuttu uraitta niṟai ñāṉattu orumūrti') transliterated via the Tamil (கூடி நீரைக் கடைந்தவாறும் அமுதம் தேவர் உண்ண அசுரர்களை வீடும் வண்ணங்கள் செய்து போன வித்தகமும்; கன்று மேய்த்து இனிது உகந்த காளாய்; நெறி எல்லாம் எடுத்து உரைத்த நிறை ஞானத்து ஒருமூர்த்தி) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar explains that the Lord is the supreme master of all beings, because He is the master even of Brahma, Yama, and the others who are themselves the lords of beings. Nammazhwar sings that He established the other gods in their places, and He Himself remains the Lord of those gods (niṟuttinān deivaṅgaḷāga a-ddeiva nāyagan tānē).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (items 9, 13, 15, 17, 29: 'niṟuttinān deivaṅgaḷāga a-ddeiva nāyagan tānē', 'inbuṟum ivviḷaiyāṭṭuḍaiyān', 'vānōr perumān māmāyan vaikunthan emperumān', 'manisarkku dēvar pōla dēvarkkum dēvan', 'ūzhi thōṟu ūzhi vaiyam kākkum āzhi nīr vaṇṇan') transliterated via the Tamil per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text. In item 15 the glossary form एम्पेरुमान् was used for 'emperumān'.

concerns.english: Thondaradippodi Azhwar says, "You stay with them and know all that is in the hearts of those who think of You" (uḷḷuvār uḷḷiṟṟellām uḍan irundu aṟidi). Sri Bhattar explains that the Lord watches over His devotees constantly, out of concern that no harm should come to them.
concerns.note: Tamil phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 28 Thondaradippodi Azhwar 'uḷḷuvār uḷḷiṟṟellām uḍan irundu aṟidi', item 30 Nammazhwar 'pul eṟumbu ādi onṟu inṟiyē') transliterated via the Tamil (உள்ளுவார் உள்ளிற்றெல்லாம் உடன் இருந்து அறிதி; புல் எறும்பு ஆதி ஒன்று இன்றியே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Periyazhwar sings of the Lord "who spread the serpent as His bed upon the white flood (of milk), and lies in His feigned sleep" (veḷḷai veḷḷattin mēl oru pāmbai meththaiyāga viriththu athan mēlē kaḷḷa niththirai koḷginṟa). His sleep is yoga nidra, in which He is thinking of the welfare of the world.
concerns.note: Periyazhwar phrase 'veḷḷai veḷḷattin mēl oru pāmbai meththaiyāga viriththu athan mēlē kaḷḷa niththirai koḷginṟa' transliterated via the Tamil (வெள்ளை வெள்ளத்தின் மேல் ஒரு பாம்பை மெத்தையாக விரித்து அதன் மேலே கள்ள நித்திரை கொள்கின்ற) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The one who is deep and mysterious, because His transcendent nature, revealed by the Pancha-Upanishad mantras, is beyond our full understanding.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrase 'ñālam uṇḍu umizhndha mālai eṇṇumāṟu aṟiya māṭṭēn' transliterated via the Tamil (ஞாலம் உண்டு உமிழ்ந்த மாலை எண்ணுமாறு அறிய மாட்டேன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar begins the Thiruvaimozhi by describing the Lord as "the one who possesses the highest goodness, above which there is nothing higher" (uyarvaṟa uyar nalam uḍaiyavan). The Lord is free from every flaw (hēya pratyanīka) and full of every good quality (kalyāṇaika tāna). These two aspects together make Him the only one fit to be called Bhagavan.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrase 'uyarvaṟa uyar nalam uḍaiyavan' (Tiruvāymoḻi 1.1.1) transliterated via the Tamil (உயர்வற உயர் நலம் உடையவன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar calls upon us to praise the lotus-eyed Lord who removes all our sins (pāva nāsanai paṅkaya taḍam kaṇṇanai paravuminō). Periyazhwar calls Him "naraka nāśan", the destroyer of hell.
concerns.note: Tamil phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 25 Nammazhwar 'pāva nāsanai paṅkaya taḍam kaṇṇanai paravuminō', Periyazhwar 'naraka nāśan') transliterated via the Tamil (பாவ நாசனை பங்கய தடம் கண்ணனை பரவுமினோ; நரக நாசன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: In the Bhishma Stava Raja of the Mahabharata, it is said, "The groups of rishis, the siddhas, the great serpents, the devas, and the divine sages came to know Narayana as the medicine for the disease of samsara." Peyazhwar says that He is the medicine, the wealth, and the nectar (marundum poruḷum amudamum tānē), and Nammazhwar calls Him the great medicine for our disease.
concerns.note: Peyazhwar phrase 'marundum poruḷum amudamum tānē' transliterated via the Tamil (மருந்தும் பொருளும் அமுதமும் தானே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar quotes the Ramayana, which describes the Lord as "nitya śrīḥ", the one with whom Lakshmi always resides. The Lord is like a garden of wish-fulfilling (kalpaka) trees, and Lakshmi is like a wish-fulfilling creeper that roams freely and joyfully in that garden. Nammazhwar describes Him as the one on whose chest the Lady of the lotus resides, declaring, "I shall not leave Him even for a moment" (agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl maṅgai uṟai mārbā).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 23 'agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl maṅgai uṟai mārbā', item 25 'thiruvin maṇāḷan') transliterated via the Tamil (அகலகில்லேன் இறையும் என்று அலர்மேல் மங்கை உறை மார்பா; திருவின் மணாளன்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The one who is ever delighted, because He is always with Sri Mahalakshmi at all times, in all places, and in all ways.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrase 'ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adhipati' (Tiruvāymoḻi 1.1.1) transliterated via the Tamil (அயர்வறும் அமரர்கள் அதிபதி) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar calls Him "the one whose fame has no equal" (nigar il pugazhāy). There are two kinds of fame: the fame that comes from wealth and position, which is temporary, and the fame that comes from following dharma, which lasts forever. The Lord's fame is of the second kind.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 5 'nigar il pugazhāy', item 21 'sēlēi kaṇṇiyarum perum selvamum nan makkaḷum mēlāt thāi thandhaiyum avarē') transliterated via the Tamil (நிகர் இல் புகழாய்; சேலேய் கண்ணியரும் பெரும் செல்வமும் நன் மக்களும் மேலாத் தாய் தந்தையும் அவரே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text. Item 3 temple names (Thiruvekka, 'Sonna Vannam Seida Perumal') rendered तिरुवेक्का and सॊन्न वण्णम् शॆय्द पेरुमाल; verify.

concerns.english: While all the wealth of this world eventually causes sorrow, the Lord is the only wealth that removes sorrow. Thirumazhisai Azhwar says, "He becomes our father, our mother, and our Lord, puts an end to our countless births, and takes us into His service" (attan āgi annai āgi āḷum empirānumāi).
concerns.note: Tamil phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 0 Thirumazhisai Azhwar 'attan āgi annai āgi āḷum empirānumāi'; Nammazhwar items 11 'ennaik koṇḍu en pāvam tannaiyum pāṟak kaitthu', 16 'ottār mikkārai ilaiyāya māyan', 31 'ulagam mūnṟu udaiyāi') transliterated via the Tamil per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text. Item 26: English gives the earlier naama as 'sūraḥ'; rendered शूरः (the 341st naama is śūraḥ); owner to confirm the English spelling.

concerns.english: Kamsa sent the asura Kesi, in the form of a horse, to kill the child Krishna, but Krishna thrust His arm into its mouth and destroyed it. Andal refers to this in the Thiruppavai, "mā vāi kīṇḍānai", the one who tore apart the mouth of the horse. Sage Vyasa himself gives this as another meaning of the name Kesava, "the slayer of Kesi."
concerns.note: Tamil phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 2 Andal 'mā vāi kīṇḍānai'; item 4 Thondaradippodi Azhwar 'paccai mā malai pōl mēni'; Nammazhwar item 10 'parugu innamudē', item 27 'dēvum epporuḷum paḍaikka pūvil nānmuganaip paḍaitta dēvan emperumān') transliterated via the Tamil per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The Sruti says, "Narayana is the supreme light" (nārāyaṇa parō jyōtiḥ). The light of a thousand suns is only a small fraction of His light. Thirumazhisai Azhwar calls Him "the light that no one can question" (sōdiyāda sōdi nī).
concerns.note: Thirumazhisai Azhwar phrase 'sōdiyāda sōdi nī' transliterated via the Tamil (சோதியாத சோதி நீ) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The one in whom all beings reside.
concerns.note: Andal phrase 'vada madurai maindanai thūya peru nīr yamunai thuṟaivanai' (Tiruppāvai 5) transliterated via the Tamil (வட மதுரை மைந்தனை தூய பெரு நீர் யமுனை துறைவனை) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The master of all the worlds, whose relationship with all beings as their master is natural and unique, and is the reason for His attachment to them.
concerns.note: Andal phrase 'unthannōdu uṟavēl namakku iṅgu ozhikka ozhiyādu' (Tiruppāvai 28) transliterated via the Tamil (உன்தன்னோடு உறவேல் நமக்கு இங்கு ஒழிக்க ஒழியாது) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: At Thirukkudanthai (Kumbakonam), the Lord is called Aaraavamudhan, the nectar that never satiates. Nammazhwar dedicates a whole decade of the Thiruvaimozhi (5.8) to Him, and calls out again and again to "my nectar that never satiates" (en ārā amudamē). It was by hearing these very pasurams sung at Kumbakonam that Sri Nathamuni was inspired to recover the Divya Prabandham.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrase 'en ārā amudamē' transliterated via the Tamil (என் ஆரா அமுதமே) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Thirumazhisai Azhwar describes the Lord as always thinking, "What more can I do for My devotees?" (un adiyārkku en seyvan enṟē irutti nī).
concerns.note: Thirumazhisai Azhwar phrase 'un adiyārkku en seyvan enṟē irutti nī' transliterated via the Tamil (உன் அடியார்க்கு என் செய்வன் என்றே இருத்தி நீ) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar, in one of the last decades of the Thiruvaimozhi, says, "I joyfully served You and obtained Your lotus feet. What more could I want, my Father?" (uṟṟēn ugandu paṇi seidu un pādam peṟṟēn).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 4 'uṟṟēn ugandu paṇi seidu un pādam peṟṟēn', item 6 'sāi koṇḍa immaiyum sādittu vānavar nāṭṭaiyum nī kaṇḍu koḷ enṟu vīḍum tarum') transliterated via the Tamil (உற்றேன் உகந்து பணி செய்து உன் பாதம் பெற்றேன்; சாய் கொண்ட இம்மையும் சாதித்து வானவர் நாட்டையும் நீ கண்டு கொள் என்று வீடும் தரும்) per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Even when He appears to be sleeping on Adisesha in the milky ocean, He is in yoga nidra, always awake and thinking of ways to help the jeevaathmas reach Him. Nammazhwar describes this as the Lord's sleep in which He is thinking of the protection of the world (ulagu aḷikkum yōga nidrai).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases quoted only in romanisation (item 10 'ulagu aḷikkum yōga nidrai', item 24 'vaikuntham puguvadu maṇṇavar vidhiyē', item 28 'uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr thinnum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan') transliterated via the Tamil per Standard §3.3; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The sound of the Panchajanya, when the Lord blows it, strikes terror into the hearts of the wicked and fills the hearts of His devotees with joy. Andal, in her Nachiyar Thirumozhi, asks the Panchajanya, which has the good fortune of touching the Lord's lips, "Does His mouth smell of camphor? Does it smell of the lotus? Tell me, O white conch!" (karpūram nāRumO kamalappū nāzhumō).
concerns.note: Andal phrase quoted in romanisation as 'karpūram nāRumO kamalappū nāzhumō' (Nāchiyār Tirumoḻi 7.1). The second 'nāzhumō' appears to be a typo in the English for 'nāṟumō' (நாறுமோ); the Hindi follows the Tamil (கற்பூரம் நாறுமோ கமலப்பூ நாறுமோ → कर्पूरम् नाऱुमो कमलप्पू नाऱुमो). The authoritative text may read 'karuppūram'; owner to verify. Item 14 Andal 'śārṅgam udaitta sara mazhai pōl' (Tiruppāvai 4) transliterated via the Tamil (சார்ங்கம் உதைத்த சர மழை போல்); verify.

concerns.english: 3. saṅkarṣaṇa - jñāna and bala - function of saṃhāra or destruction The vibhava is that group of manifestations that Bhagavān takes in the form of God, man, animal, etc. (sura, nara, tiryagādi). Vibhava is of two kinds:
concerns.note: English item runs two paragraphs together: '... function of saṃhāra or destruction The vibhava is that group of manifestations ...' (missing full stop/paragraph break after 'destruction'). Translated as one item to keep paragraph parity; owner to fix the English.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar's words are "taiḥ bhujyatē sukhēna anubhūyatē iti bhōjanam", "He is enjoyed with delight by His devotees." The Lord makes the objects of this world fit to be enjoyed, and when His devotee rises above the desire for worldly things, He becomes Himself the object of their enjoyment. Nammazhwar says that for him, the Lord is the food he eats, the water he drinks, and the betel he chews (uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr thinnum veṭṭilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar line 'uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr thinnum veṭṭilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan' (Tiruvāymoḻi 6.7.1) written in Tamil as உண்ணும் சோறு பருகுநீர் தின்னும் வெற்றிலையும் எல்லாம் கண்ணன்; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: One explanation of the name is "the one who made Bali give up (vāmayati) his pride". Another is "the one with a charming small form" (vāmō valgutvam asya asti). The Lord came to Bali as a young brahmachari student, so beautiful that Bali could not refuse Him anything. Periyazhwar and the other Azhwars sing of this "little brahmachari" (kuṟaḷ māṇi) with great delight.
concerns.note: Tamil phrases quoted in romanisation: 'kuṟaḷ māṇi' (குறள் மாணி) and Andal's 'ōṅgi ulagaḷanda uttaman' (Tiruppāvai 3; ஓங்கி உலகளந்த உத்தமன், item 3) written in Tamil script; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad says, "This Self is honey to all beings" (ayamātmā sarvēṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu). Periyazhwar calls Him "the Lord who is sweeter than honey" (thēnil iniya pirānē). From the next name, Sri Bhattar describes the Lord's six divine qualities: knowledge, strength, lordship, valour, power, and splendour.
concerns.note: Periyazhwar phrase 'thēnil iniya pirānē' written in Tamil as தேனில் இனிய பிரானே; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: When the Milk Ocean was churned, Sri Mahalakshmi rose from it. While all the devas waited and watched, She chose the Lord, and He welcomed Her to reside on His chest. Nammazhwar describes Her declaring that She will not leave Him even for a moment (agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl maṅgai uṟai mārbā).
concerns.note: Tamil quotations in romanisation written in Tamil script: Nammazhwar 'agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl maṅgai uṟai mārbā' (Tiruvāymoḻi 6.10.10; அகலகில்லேன் இறையும் என்று அலர்மேல் மங்கை உறை மார்பா) and Andal 'kuṟai onṟum illādha gōvindā' (Tiruppāvai 28; item 12, குறைவொன்றுமில்லாத கோவிந்தா). Verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: The one who is constantly blessing His devotees.
concerns.note: Thiruppanazhwar line 'en amudhinaik kaṇḍa kaṇgaḷ maṟṟonṟinaik kāṇāvē' (Amalanādipirān 10) written in Tamil as என் அமுதினைக் கண்ட கண்கள் மற்றொன்றினைக் காணாவே; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: For those filled with Taamasa Guna, the Lord hides Himself until the Taamasa Guna is wholly relieved and then will show the devotee the right path.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrase 'mayarvaṟa madhinalam aruḷinan' (Tiruvāymoḻi 1.1.1) written in Tamil as மயர்வற மதிநலம் அருளினன்; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Nammazhwar describes how the Lord, as the inner controller of Rudra, burnt down the three cities of the asuras and gave knowledge to the devas (puram oru mūnṟu eritthu amararkkum aṟivu iyandhu). By destroying their cities, He removed the fears that came upon the devas.
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrase 'puram oru mūnṟu eritthu amararkkum aṟivu iyandhu' (Tiruvāymoḻi 1.1.8) written in Tamil as புரம் ஒரு மூன்று எரித்து அமரர்க்கும் அறிவு இயந்து; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Andal sings in the Thiruppavai of the Lord who "went there and destroyed beautiful Lanka in the south" (senṟu angu then ilangai seṟṟāi). Periyazhwar sings of how He went and cut off the thousand arms of Banasura. The Lord's valour is always used to go to His devotees' aid.
concerns.note: Tamil quotations in romanisation written in Tamil script, all to verify: Andal 'senṟu angu then ilangai seṟṟāi' (Tiruppāvai 24; சென்று அங்குத் தென்இலங்கை செற்றாய்); item 22 Thiruppanazhwar 'ayanaip paḍaitthadhōr ezhil undhi' (Amalanādipirān 4; அயனைப் படைத்ததோர் எழில் உந்தி); item 32 Nammazhwar 'vīṟṟirundhu Ezh ulagum thanik kōl sella ALum ammān' (Tiruvāymoḻi 4.5.1; வீற்றிருந்து ஏழுலகும் தனிக்கோல் செல்ல ஆளும் அம்மான்).

concerns.english: Thiruppaanazhwar sings of "those great, long eyes with red streaks, which have driven me mad" (seyya vāya aiyō ennaic cindhai kavarndhadhuvē). In the Sundara Kandam, Hanuman describes Rama as "rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ", Rama with eyes like lotus petals.
concerns.note: English-source mismatch (already recorded for hi): the quoted line 'seyya vāya aiyō ennaic cindhai kavarndhadhuvē' (Amalanādipirān 7, செய்ய வாய் ஐயோ என்னைச் சிந்தை கவர்ந்ததுவே) is about the Lord's red mouth, but the English glosses it as the long red-streaked eyes. Translated faithfully; owner to correct the English.

concerns.english: Garuda is said to be the embodiment of the Vedas, and so the Lord's vehicle is worthy of the highest reverence. Nammazhwar calls the Lord "the one who rides on the bird" (puḷḷūrdhi).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases in romanisation written in Tamil script, all to verify: 'puḷḷūrdhi' (புள்ளூர்தி); item 26 'thiruc ceyya kamalak kaṇṇum sevvāyum sevvadiyum' (திருச்செய்ய கமலக் கண்ணும் செவ்வாயும் செவ்வடியும்); item 34 'etthiṟam! uralinōdu iṇaindhirundhu Engiya eḷivē' (Tiruvāymoḻi 1.3.1; எத்திறம்! உரலினோடு இணைந்திருந்து ஏங்கிய எளிவே).

concerns.english: Nammazhwar sings of the Lord "whose soft feet are pressed by the Lady of the lotus and by the Lady of the earth" (malar magaḷ maṟṟum maṇ magaḷ pidikkum mel adiyān).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases in romanisation written in Tamil script, all to verify: 'malar magaḷ maṟṟum maṇ magaḷ pidikkum mel adiyān' (மலர்மகள் மற்றும் மண்மகள் பிடிக்கும் மெல்லடியான்); item 12 'palapala māya mayakkugaḷāl inbuṟum iv viḷaiyāṭṭudaiyān' (பலபல மாய மயக்குகளால் இன்புறும் இவ்விளையாட்டுடையான்); item 26 'viṇṇavarkku eṇṇal ariyān' (விண்ணவர்க்கு எண்ணல் அரியான்); item 28 'kākkum iyalvinan kaṇṇa perumān' (காக்கும் இயல்வினன் கண்ணபெருமான்).

concerns.english: Because He is complete in every respect, there is no room in Him for likes and dislikes, wants and desires. Thiruvalluvar describes the Lord as "the one who has neither desire nor aversion" (vēṇḍudal vēṇḍāmai ilān). Meditating on this naama helps us move towards that state ourselves.
concerns.note: Thiruvalluvar (Kural 4) phrase 'vēṇḍudal vēṇḍāmai ilān' written in Tamil as வேண்டுதல் வேண்டாமை இலான்; verify against the authoritative text.

concerns.english: Sri Bhattar quotes the Bala Kandam: "The son of king Dasaratha, endowed with world-wide renown" (pṛthuśrīḥ pārthivātmajaḥ), and "Among them, Rama was the most renowned in the world" (tēṣām atiyaśā lōkē rāmaḥ). Nammazhwar calls Him "the one whose fame has no equal" (nigar il pugazhāy).
concerns.note: Nammazhwar phrases in romanisation written in Tamil script, to verify: 'nigar il pugazhāy' (நிகரில் புகழாய்) and item 23 'tēnum pālum kannalum amudumāgit tittippa' (தேனும் பாலும் கன்னலும் அமுதுமாகித் தித்திப்ப).

concerns.english: This naama occurs again as the 821st naama. Sri Bhattar explains that He knows that He is the inner controller of everything, and that He is Himself the best dharma, the best means, and the best goal. Thirumangai Azhwar addresses Him as "You who know everything in the world" (ulagattu ellām aṟivīr).
concerns.note: Thirumangai Azhwar phrase 'ulagattu ellām aṟivīr' written in Tamil as உலகத்து எல்லாம் அறிவீர்; verify against the authoritative text.
